newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says ETA suspect was not tortured.
newsitem.headline: Spain says ETA suspect was not tortured.

text.p: Spain's government said on Saturday a forensic report provided proof that a suspected ETA killer had not been tortured during interrogation by the police.
The suspect, Fernando Elejalde, was taken semi-conscious to hospital from police cells on Thursday, two days after being captured by police.

"As we hoped, we have received with great satisfaction a first report completed by the forensic doctor that effectively excuses the police of any kind of maltreatment," said Foreign Minister Abel Matutes.
"It appears that this man's injuries were sustained during his arrest," he told local radio.
But defence lawyers, who were allowed to see their client for the first time, said Elejalde maintained he had suffered his injuries in police custody.
"None of the injuries to his body or lower back are a result of the arrest," lawyer Ainhoa Baigliot told Europa Press Television.

The hospital in the Basque city of San Sebastian said Elejalde had four crushed vertebrae in his lower back, internal bleeding from a ruptured kidney, a perforated eardrum and bruises covering his face and body.

Police arrested Elejalde, 29, after an extended gun battle with police as he ran from the scene of the killing of prison psychologist Javier Garcia Elosegui in San Sebastian. Another attacker, a woman, escaped.
The Foreign Ministry said Elejalde was injured when he was hit by a car as he ran from police and fought with them when they arrested him.
A Supreme Court judge ruled that Elejalde should be held without bail on charges including the murder of Elosegui, local media reported.
But, after a further two-hour bedside interrogation, the judge lifted a solitary confinement order on Elejalde and his brother and lawyers visited him under police watch.
The lawyers said he claimed he had been arrested peacefully. "He told us that the blows that he received started when he arrived at the police station," Baigliot said.
He said Elejalde, who was taken to an emergency clinic two hours after his arrest on Tuesday, reported that police continued to beat him on Wednesday and Thursday.
But newspapers said forensic doctor Carmen Baigorri, who examined Elejalde during his detention, reported that the wounds treated on Thursday were the same as those noted two hours after his arrest.
The daily El Pais said Baigorri was convinced there were no signs of torture or maltreatment.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja is due to report to parliament on Monday on Elejalde's arrest.

Earlier this week, he had to explain in parliament what happened to an ETA suspect who was found hanged in his prison cell with his feet and hands tied, facts that were not immediately released by the government.
About 800 people have been killed in ETA's 29-year guerrilla war for an independent Basque state.
